newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan vice-president to visit Nicaragua.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan vice-president to visit Nicaragua.

text.p: Taiwan Vice-President Lien Chan will visit Nicaragua for the inauguration of President-elect Arnoldo Aleman on January 10, Taiwan's presidential office said on Friday.
Lien, who doubles as Taiwan's premier, will attend the inauguration on behalf of President Lee Teng-hui, state-run news media quoted presidential spokesman Chen Hsi-fan as saying.
Chen said the foreign ministry was ironing out details and dates of the visit. He did not elaborate.

Nicaragua is one of only 30 countries -- mostly poor states in Africa and central America -- that recognise Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government instead of the rival communist Chinese government in Beijing.
Taiwan and China split after a civil war in 1949.
Beijing considers Taiwan a renegade province and seeks to isolate the island completely from international arenas until it can be reunified under mainland sovereignty.

Taiwan newspapers had reported that Lien decided to visit Nicaragua out of fear that Taipei's allies may be tempted to ditch Taipei for Beijing after South Africa announced in November it would make such a switch in 1997.
Pretoria had been Taiwan's biggest ally.
